operators.name: stack_relu_forward

parameters.name: x
parameters.shape: [512, 3, 256, 256] (input tensor shape as provided by task)

returns.shape: [512, 4, 3, 256, 256] (output shape: input shape with a new dimension of size num_channels inserted at stack_dim)

semantics: Applies torch.relu elementwise to the input tensor x.
Then stacks num_channels copies of the relu result along dimension stack_dim.
The output has shape [batch, num_channels, channels, height, width] when stack_dim=1.
The input tensor is assumed to be on CUDA and float32; the function allocates a contiguous output tensor of the appropriate shape.
The order of tensor copying follows torch.stack semantics: output[..., i, ...] = relu(x) for i in range(num_channels) at the stack dimension.
The operation is idempotent w.r.t. self.stack parameter; that parameter is not used for computation.

reference_steps.source: x = torch.stack([self.relu(x) for _ in range(self.num_channels)], dim=self.stack_dim)
semantics: Creates a list of num_channels identical relu(x) tensors.
Stacks them along the dimension self.stack_dim (which is 1).
The resulting tensor has shape [512, 4, 3, 256, 256] for the given input shape.
The output is on CUDA and float32, contiguous with stride [786432, 196608, 65536, 256, 1].
Returns the tensor produced in step_001 unchanged.
The returned tensor is the same object as the stacked tensor.
